stem: An analyst wants `Runtime` to use an average every time it is dropped into any new view of the workbook. Where should the default be changed?

options.text: In the `Runtime` pill's menu on the shelf, under Measure
options.rationale: This changes the aggregation for that one pill in that one view, not for future uses.

options.text: In the Analysis menu, by clearing Aggregate Measures
options.rationale: This switches the view to one mark per row. It doesn't set a default aggregation.

options.text: In the Data pane, right-click `Runtime` and choose Default Properties > Aggregation
options.rationale: The Data pane setting is the default that applies to every new use of the field in the workbook.

options.text: In the Marks card, by dragging `Runtime` to Detail
options.rationale: Detail adds a dimension to the level of detail; it doesn't change a measure's default aggregation.

explanation: Each measure gets a default aggregation when you connect to the data. You change it for one view on the pill, or for the whole workbook in the Data pane under Default Properties > Aggregation.

stem: After clearing Aggregate Measures on the Analysis menu, what does a view of `Minutes Watched` against `Runtime` show?

options.text: A separate mark for every row of data
options.rationale: A disaggregated view draws one mark per row, like a scatterplot of raw records.

options.text: One mark per member of every dimension in the Data pane
options.rationale: Marks follow the dimensions placed in the view, and none are needed here. Aggregation isn't involved in that rule.

options.text: A single mark that sums every row in the data source
options.rationale: That is what aggregation with no dimensions gives; clearing the option does the opposite.

options.text: The same marks as before, with `SUM` replaced by `AVG` on each pill
options.rationale: Clearing the option doesn't change a pill's aggregation; it removes aggregation altogether.

explanation: Aggregate Measures controls whether Tableau combines rows into marks. When it is cleared, the view is disaggregated and each row of data gets its own mark.

stem: A view shows `SUM(Minutes Watched)` per `Plan`. A manager asks for the typical length of a session instead of the total. What is the simplest change?

options.text: Drag `Plan` from Columns to Detail so that the totals shrink
options.rationale: Moving a dimension changes the level of detail but the pill would still be summed.

options.text: Convert `Minutes Watched` to a dimension so that it is not summed
options.rationale: A dimension would no longer be a measure on the axis, and nothing would describe a typical session.

options.text: Clear Aggregate Measures so that the totals disappear
options.rationale: The view would then show one mark per session row, not a typical value per plan.

options.text: Change the aggregation of the pill to Average or Median
options.rationale: A sum grows with the number of sessions, whereas an average or median describes a typical one.

explanation: Choose the aggregation to fit the question. SUM answers 'how much in total'; Average or Median answers 'how long is a typical session'. The pill's menu, under Measure, offers them.

stem: A header in a view shows an asterisk (*) next to a `Genre` value after `Genre` was aggregated as Attribute. What does the asterisk mean?

options.text: The field contains null values that were removed from the view
options.rationale: Nulls appear as Null members, not as an asterisk, and ATTR isn't about missing data.

options.text: The group contains more than one value for the field
options.rationale: ATTR returns a value only when the group has exactly one; otherwise it shows an asterisk.

options.text: The data source returned an error when the view was drawn
options.rationale: The asterisk is a normal result of ATTR and not an error.

options.text: The member was filtered out but kept in the view as a placeholder
options.rationale: Filtering removes members from the view; it doesn't create asterisks.

explanation: Attribute (`ATTR`) returns a value only if it's the only one in the group. When the group has several values, Tableau shows an asterisk instead.

stem: Which aggregations can an analyst apply to a dimension such as `Country`, creating a temporary measure? (Choose 3 answers.)

options.text: Sum
options.rationale: Sum needs numbers, and `Country` holds text, so it isn't offered.

options.text: Count (Distinct)
options.rationale: Count (Distinct) is available for dimensions, as in `COUNTD(Country)`.

options.text: Average
options.rationale: Average needs numbers, and `Country` holds text, so it isn't offered.

options.text: Attribute
options.rationale: Attribute is one of the aggregations offered for dimensions.

options.text: Median
options.rationale: Median needs numbers, and `Country` holds text, so it isn't offered.

options.text: Maximum
options.rationale: Maximum is offered for dimensions, as is Minimum.

explanation: A dimension can be aggregated with Minimum, Maximum, Count, Count (Distinct) or Attribute. Tableau then creates a temporary measure column.

stem: Which statements about default aggregations are correct? (Choose 3 answers.)

options.text: Changing a pill's aggregation updates the field's default for the whole workbook.
options.rationale: The workbook-wide default is set in the Data pane, not through a pill.

options.text: Tableau sets each measure's default aggregation when it connects to the data.
options.rationale: The default is set at connection time, and for numbers it is usually a sum.

options.text: Every measure uses `SUM` as its default, whatever its data.
options.rationale: SUM is the usual default for numbers, but it isn't the only one.

options.text: Changing the aggregation on a pill affects that pill in that view only.
options.rationale: A pill's menu change is local; other views and the Data pane default stay as they were.

options.text: Clearing Aggregate Measures resets every default aggregation to `SUM`.
options.rationale: It turns aggregation off for the view, but it doesn't alter defaults.

options.text: A published data source's default aggregations can't be changed in the workbook.
options.rationale: They are decided where the data source is published.

explanation: Defaults are set by Tableau on connection and can be changed per pill or in the Data pane. They can't be changed for a published data source, because the publisher decides them.

stem: An analyst connects to a published data source and tries to change a measure's default aggregation in the Data pane. What is the situation?

options.text: It works, but only for the first worksheet in the workbook
options.rationale: Default Properties apply workbook-wide when they can be set, and not just to one sheet.

options.text: It works if the analyst first clears Aggregate Measures on the Analysis menu
options.rationale: Clearing the option disaggregates the view; it doesn't unlock default settings.

options.text: The default can't be set there, because the publisher decides it
options.rationale: Default aggregations of a published data source are controlled where it is published.

options.text: It works if the field is first converted from a measure to a dimension
options.rationale: A dimension has no default aggregation to set, and the restriction wouldn't change.

explanation: Tableau doesn't let you set default aggregations for published data sources. The analyst can still change the aggregation on a pill in a view.

stem: A view shows `SUM(Minutes Watched)` as one bar per `Plan`. An analyst drops `Device` on Color. What happens?

options.text: Each plan's bar splits into one segment per device, and the bar heights stay the same
options.rationale: The measure is computed for each plan and device, and the segments add up to the plan total.

options.text: Each plan's bar is replaced by one bar per device, side by side, and a header is added
options.rationale: Color adds marks without adding headers, so the bars are stacked and not split into new headers.

options.text: The bars become averages across devices because a second dimension is present
options.rationale: Adding a dimension doesn't change the aggregation; the pill is still `SUM`.

options.text: The bars shrink because `Device` filters out some sessions
options.rationale: A field on Color groups rows; it doesn't remove any.

explanation: Every dimension in the view, including those on Color, increases the level of detail. Because SUM is additive, the segments add back up to the former bars.

stem: After a dimension was dropped on the Marks card, the numbers in a bar chart became smaller and no new headers appeared. Which concept explains it?

options.text: The default aggregation of the measure was changed to Average
options.rationale: Changing an aggregation is done on a pill or in the Data pane, not by dropping a field on the Marks card.

options.text: The view was disaggregated, so each mark shows one row
options.rationale: Disaggregation is set on the Analysis menu and doesn't come from adding a field.

options.text: A measure filter removed the rows with the largest values
options.rationale: Filters aren't involved; no field was added to the Filters shelf.

options.text: The level of detail increased, so each total was split into more groups
options.rationale: A dimension on Color, Size, Label or Detail adds groups without adding headers.

explanation: Dimensions on the Marks card count towards the level of detail just like those on Rows or Columns. More groups means more marks and smaller values.

stem: A scatterplot of `Sessions (Count)` against `SUM(Minutes Watched)` shows a single circle for all of Driftlight. Where should the analyst drag `Country` to get one circle per country, without a legend or new headers?

options.text: Color on the Marks card
options.rationale: Color would split the marks, but it would also add a legend.

options.text: Detail on the Marks card
options.rationale: Detail adds a dimension to the level of detail without colour, size or headers.

options.text: The Filters shelf
options.rationale: A filter chooses which rows are kept; it doesn't split the marks per country.

options.text: The Columns shelf
options.rationale: Columns would turn `Country` into headers and replace the continuous axis with it.

explanation: Detail is the Marks card property for adding a dimension to the level of detail without encoding it visually. Each member of the field then gets its own mark.

stem: An analyst removes `Device` from a view that shows `SUM(Minutes Watched)` per `Plan` and `Device`. What happens to the measure?

options.text: It is recomputed over the larger groups, one per plan
options.rationale: Removing a dimension merges groups again, and the aggregate is calculated over the merged rows.

options.text: It stays computed per device, which is simply hidden from the view
options.rationale: The level of detail follows the dimensions in the view, so nothing stays hidden.

options.text: It becomes an average of the earlier device values
options.rationale: Tableau recomputes from the underlying rows and doesn't average earlier results.

options.text: It becomes null until the analyst re-adds a dimension
options.rationale: A view with fewer dimensions is valid; with no dimension, it simply shows one overall mark.

explanation: The marks follow the dimensions in the view. Take one away, and Tableau aggregates the measure over the bigger groups.

stem: A hypothetical table has three sessions for one plan: two on Mobile with 10 and 20 minutes, and one on TV with 60 minutes. With `Plan` and `Device` in the view, `AVG(Minutes Watched)` shows 15 for Mobile and 60 for TV. What does it show when `Device` is removed and only `Plan` remains?

options.rationale: This averages the two device averages, but Tableau averages the underlying rows.
This adds up all three sessions' minutes, which is a `SUM`, not an `AVG`.
The average of all three rows is (10 + 20 + 60) / 3 = 30.
This adds the device averages, which isn't what any aggregation does here.

explanation: An AVG isn't additive: the plan average comes from all rows in the larger group, not from the device averages. This is why SUM and COUNT split cleanly but AVG doesn't.

stem: Which actions increase the number of marks in a bar chart of `SUM(Minutes Watched)` per `Plan`? (Choose 3 answers.)

options.text: Drop `Country` on Detail
options.rationale: Detail adds a dimension to the level of detail and so more marks.

options.text: Change the `SUM` to `AVG` on the pill
options.rationale: This changes the calculation, but the number of marks stays the same.

options.text: Drop `Device` on Color
options.rationale: A dimension on Color adds a mark per device within each plan.

options.text: Set `Minutes Watched` to Average under Default Properties > Aggregation
options.rationale: This changes the default aggregation, not the dimensions that form the groups.

options.text: Drop `Genre` on Rows
options.rationale: A new dimension on a shelf multiplies the member combinations.

explanation: Marks come from the combinations of members of the dimensions in the view. Changing an aggregation changes the values on the marks, not how many there are.

stem: A view shows a measure per `Plan`. When `Device` is added on Color, for which aggregations do the per-device values add back up to the per-plan value? (Choose 2 answers.)

options.text: `AVG(Minutes Watched)`
options.rationale: Averaging per-device averages doesn't give the plan average.

options.text: `SUM(Minutes Watched)`
options.rationale: The pieces of a sum add up to the former total.

options.text: `MEDIAN(Minutes Watched)`
options.rationale: A median of medians isn't the overall median.

options.text: `Sessions (Count)`
options.rationale: Row counts are additive, so the device counts add up to the plan count.

options.text: `COUNTD(Subscriber ID)`
options.rationale: A subscriber may watch on several devices, so the distinct counts can add up to more than the plan's.

explanation: SUM and COUNT are additive, so splitting by a dimension gives parts that sum to the old total. AVG, MEDIAN and COUNTD aren't additive.
